detail.title: LLM Reasoning Blind Spot Identification
detail.question: To what extent can Large Language Models systematically identify and navigate 'blind spots' in their own generated thought structures?
detail.reason: Current reasoning methods often rely on previously generated logical directions, creating unexplored solution spaces; identifying these blind spots is critical to improving model reliability.

detail.title: Synthesis of LLM Reasoning Blind Spots and Epistemic Awareness
detail.summary: Procedural blind spots in reasoning, such as unexplored solution space, are actively managed through iterative expansion methods like Thought Space Explorer (TSE), whereas epistemic knowledge gaps require reflective and uncertainty-aware mechanisms. The two concepts represent complementary approaches to model reliability.
detail.reason: This notebook synthesizes distinct but related literature streams regarding search-space limitations (blind spots) and epistemic self-assessment in LLMs.

detail.title: Revision of LLM Reasoning Blind Spots and Epistemic Awareness
detail.summary: LLM 'blind spots' are increasingly identifiable as failures in heuristic search where the model fixates on local optima. This synthesis connects EACL 2026 reasoning findings with formal search limitations, suggesting that systematic improvement requires explicit navigation of the search space rather than implicit prediction.
detail.reason: Revising reasoning blind spot analysis to incorporate classical search literature.
